These tumours are frequently composed of pleomorphic spindle cells arranged in fascicles or disorganized sheets.

The tumour is metastatic to lung. This primitive tumour has a biphasic growth pattern, composed of nests and cords of primitive epithelial cells intermixed with primitive spindle stromal cells. Mitoses are identified.
This primitive tumour with a biphasic growth pattern is composed of nests of primitive epithelial follicular cells intermixed with primitive spindle stromal cells.

Thyroblastoma is an embryonal neoplasm that resembles thyroid within the first trimester of prenatal development. It is composed of distinct cellular components including a component represented by fetal-type TTF1+/PAX8+/very focal thyroglobulin+ primitive-type thyroid follicles, and by primitive small oval to spindle cells, arranged as irregularly communicating solid aggregates with mitotic activity.

This paediatric poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma has a predominant solid component with scattered small follicle-like structures highlighted by thyroglobulin immunohistochemistry.

This large thyroid tumour in a child is composed of small cells with small uniform nuclei. Paediatric PDTC typically carries germline DICER1 variants and lacks the molecular alterations characteristic of adult-type PDTC.

title: Table 8.02 Summary of histopathological features in selected DICER1-related tumour predisposition syndrome–associated tumours
source: All authors, especially the pathologists, worked on this table that was created especially for this volume
tablehtml:
Conditions

Key histopathological features

Diagnostic studies

Pleuropulmonary blastoma (PPB)

Type I (cystic)

Type Ir (cystic)

Type II (cystic and solid)

Type III (solid)

Multilocular lung cyst with septa that contain clusters or layers of primitive rhabdomyoblastic cells, type I PPB, or, if lacking primitive cells, type Ir. Expansion of the primitive cell component into visible solid nodules signifies type II. Purely solid tumours are type III. Solid components are typically multipatterned with embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, malignant cartilage, spindle cell sarcoma, and primitive blastema. Anaplasia is common.

n/a

Thyroid neoplasia

Benign clonal follicular cell–derived nodules

Differentiated thyroid carcinoma

Poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma

Follicular nodular disease with features of solid and/or cystic growth. Follicular adenomas with papillary architecture which are characterized by intrafollicular centripetal papillary architecture may occur in the absence of clinical or subclinical hyperthyroidism. DICER1-related differentiated thyroid carcinomas comprising follicular neoplasm with invasive growth and/or nuclear features of papillary thyroid carcinoma. Poorly differentiated thyroid carcinomas, which may include remnants of differentiated thyroid carcinoma, are composed of tumour cells with solid, insular, or trabecular growth patterns, high mitotic count (≥ 3 mitoses/mm2), and/or necrosis.

n/a

Renal neoplasia

Cystic nephroma (CN)

Anaplastic sarcoma of kidney (ASK)

Circumscribed cystic masses in the kidney with septa that are often collagenous and chronically inflamed is typical of CN. Similarly to PPB, solid, multipatterned sarcomatous nodules can develop in CN, which, before linking to DICER1 pathogenic variants, was termed ASK.

n/a

Ovarian neoplasia

Sertoli–Leydig cell tumour (SLCT)

Gynandroblastoma

Solid and/or cystic and solid tumours composed of diffuse, nested, corded, and tubular arrangements of Sertoli cells, clusters of Leydig cells, and sometimes heterologous elements such as mucinous glandular epithelium or rhabdomyoblastic elements. Tumours with elements resembling juvenile granulosa cell tumour with cystic follicles have been referred to as gynandroblastoma but this may be simply a growth pattern within SLCT resembling juvenile granulosa cell tumour {32815828}.

Variable positivity with sex cord markers such as inhibin, calretinin, CD56, SF1

Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma

Uterine cervix embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma

Uterus, ovary, fallopian tubes

Other sites

In subepithelial locations such as the uterine cervix, primitive rhabdomyoblastic cells form a subepithelial layer, i.e. cambium layer, and grossly the tumour typically has a multinodular, botryoid (grape-like) appearance. Larger, more invasive tumours are composed of hypocellular and hypercellular areas containing spindle, stellate, and ovoid-shaped rhabdomyoblasts in a pale-staining oedematous to myxoid matrix. Variable degrees of visible skeletal muscle differentiation may be present with cytoplasmic cross striations. Nodules of cartilage may also be present.

Cells within cellular areas are desmin+ with variable numbers of cells showing nuclear staining for myogenin and myoD1

Nasal chondromesenchymal hamartoma

Cystic epithelial tumour of the nasal cavity and sinus lined by sinonasal mucosa and often containing nodules of cartilage.

 

Ciliary body medulloepithelioma

Intraocular tumour composed of primitive cells arising most often from the ciliary body. May be well differentiated or poorly differentiated. Cartilage nodules may be present.

 

Pituitary blastoma

Variable admixture of primitive blastemal cells, adenohypophysial neuroendocrine cells, and Rathke pouch epithelium, resembling fetal pituitary.

EZH2+, PRAME+/−, LIN28A+/−, variable Ki-67 labelling index

Blastema: Negative for most markers

Adenohypophysial neuroendocrine cells: variable reactivity for adenohypophysial transcription factors including TPIT (most common), PIT1, and SF1, and the adenohypophysial cell lineage hormones

Epithelium: cytokeratin+, EMA+

Primary intracranial sarcoma, DICER1 mutant

Variable pleomorphic, spindle cell, rhabdomyosarcomatous, and/or small round cell sarcoma patterns; multinucleated giant cells are common, eosinophilic granular inclusions are common, and hyaline cartilage is present in a small subset; limited invasion of adjacent CNS tissue may mimic gliosarcoma.

Reticulin and collagen IV–rich basement membrane; PAS+ eosinophilic globules; myogenic (desmin, SMA, and/or myogenin) expression is common but often limited; TLE1+; H3 p.Lys27me3 loss is common; p53+ in a subset; ATRX loss in a subset

Pineoblastoma

Similar to pineoblastoma not related to DICER1, a primitive round cell tumour, variable Homer Wright and/or Flexner–Wintersteiner rosettes.

Synaptophysin+, NFP+/−, chromogranin+/−, LIN28A−, Ki-67 labelling index high

Embryonal tumour with multilayered rosettes (ETMR), DICER1 mutant

Similar to C19MC-altered ETMR; variable mixtures of primitive small round cells, multilayered true rosettes, neuropil-rich foci with neuronal differentiation (neuroblastoma-like), and medulloepithelioma-like features with structures resembling the neural tube (rare).

LIN28A+, synaptophysin/NFP/NeuN+ (mostly neuropil-rich areas), vimentin+, nestin+, EMA+/−, CD99+/−, D2-40+/−, GFAP− (may be + in rare cells), cytokeratin− (may be + in medulloepithelioma-like foci), SMARCB1 (INI1) is retained, SMARCA4 (BRG1) is retained

Wilms tumour, juvenile polyps

Similar to versions not related to DICER1
